--- page ---
// This starter uses client state for its pointer effect. When replacing it,
// remove 'use client' unless the new page needs browser APIs, event handlers,
// or React client hooks.
'use client'

import { useState, type CSSProperties, type PointerEvent } from 'react'

export default function HomePage() {
  const [hovering, setHovering] = useState(false)
  const [cursor, setCursor] = useState({ x: 0, y: 0 })

  const handlePointerMove = (event: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const rect = event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect()
    setCursor({ x: event.clientX - rect.left, y: event.clientY - rect.top })
  }

  // The hover layer is the same dot grid scaled up, revealed only within a soft
  // circle that follows the cursor — so dots appear to bloom under the pointer.
  const mask = `radial-gradient(circle at ${cursor.x}px ${cursor.y}px, #000 72px, transparent 120px)`

  const container: CSSProperties = {
    position: 'relative',
    width: '100%',
    minHeight: '100vh',
    overflow: 'hidden',
    backgroundColor: '#f8fbff',
  }
  const dots: CSSProperties = {
    position: 'absolute',
    inset: 0,
    backgroundImage:
      'radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(157, 200, 255, 0.52) 1.2px, transparent 1.4px)',
    backgroundPosition: 'center',
    backgroundSize: '18px 18px',
  }
  const dotsHover: CSSProperties = {
    position: 'absolute',
    inset: 0,
    backgroundImage:
      'radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(157, 200, 255, 0.52) 2.16px, transparent 2.36px)',
    backgroundPosition: 'center',
    backgroundSize: '18px 18px',
    opacity: hovering ? 1 : 0,
    maskImage: mask,
    WebkitMaskImage: mask,
  }

  return (
    <main
      style={container}
      onPointerEnter={() => setHovering(true)}
      onPointerMove={handlePointerMove}
      onPointerLeave={() => setHovering(false)}
    >
      <div style={dots} />
      <div style={dotsHover} />
    </main>
  )
}
--- layout ---
import React from "react"
import type { Metadata } from "next"
import Script from "next/script"
import { BodyCustomCode, renderHeadCustomCode } from "@/lib/make-custom-code"
import {
  makeSiteSettings,
  sanitizeHtmlAttribute,
} from "@/lib/make-site-settings"
import "./styles.css"

const defaultTitle = "figma-make-app"
const title = makeSiteSettings.title ?? defaultTitle
const description =
  makeSiteSettings.description ??
  "Built with Next.js, Payload CMS, and Tailwind CSS"
const favicon = makeSiteSettings.icons?.icon
const socialImage = makeSiteSettings.openGraph?.image
const googleAnalyticsId = sanitizeHtmlAttribute(
  makeSiteSettings.analytics?.googleAnalyticsId,
)

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  metadataBase: new URL(
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL || "http://localhost:3000",
  ),
  title,
  description,
  robots:
    makeSiteSettings.robots?.index === false
      ? { follow: false, index: false }
      : undefined,
  icons: favicon ? { icon: favicon } : undefined,
  openGraph: {
    title,
    description,
    images: socialImage ? [socialImage] : undefined,
  },
  twitter: socialImage
    ? {
        card: "summary_large_image",
        images: [socialImage],
      }
    : undefined,
}

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode
}) {
  const language = sanitizeHtmlAttribute(makeSiteSettings.language) || "en"
  const addBypassLinks = makeSiteSettings.accessibility?.addBypassLinks === true
  const customScripts = makeSiteSettings.customScripts

  return (
    <html lang={language}>
      <head>
        {renderHeadCustomCode(customScripts?.headStart, "head-start")}
        {renderHeadCustomCode(customScripts?.headEnd, "head-end")}
      </head>
      <body className="min-h-screen bg-white text-zinc-950 antialiased">
        <BodyCustomCode html={customScripts?.bodyStart} />
        {addBypassLinks && (
          <a className="figma-bypass-link" href="#root">
            Skip to content
          </a>
        )}
        <div id="root" tabIndex={-1}>
          {children}
        </div>
        {googleAnalyticsId && (
          <>
            <Script
              src={`https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=${googleAnalyticsId}`}
              strategy="afterInteractive"
            />
            <Script id="figma-google-analytics" strategy="afterInteractive">
              {`
window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}
gtag('js', new Date());
gtag('config', ${JSON.stringify(googleAnalyticsId)});
`}
            </Script>
          </>
        )}
        <BodyCustomCode html={customScripts?.bodyEnd} />
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}

--- src/lib/payload.ts
import { getPayload } from "payload"
import config from "@payload-config"
import type { Config } from "@/payload-types"

type CollectionSlug = keyof Config["collections"]

/**
 * Get the Payload instance configured for this project.
 * Use this in server components and route handlers.
 */
export async function getPayloadClient() {
  const payloadConfig = await config
  return getPayload({ config: payloadConfig })
}

/**
 * Find a single document by slug in any collection.
 * Returns the document if found, or null if not found.
 *
 * Use this shared helper instead of duplicating slug lookup logic
 * in each route file. Call `notFound()` from `next/navigation`
 * when this returns null.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * import { findBySlug } from '@/lib/payload'
 * import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
 *
 * export default async function ArticlePage({ params }) {
 *   const { slug } = await params
 *   const article = await findBySlug('articles', slug)
 *   if (!article) notFound()
 *   return <Article data={article} />
 * }
 * ```
 */
export async function findBySlug<T extends CollectionSlug>(
  collection: T,
  slug: string,
  options?: {
    /** Include draft documents (default: false, only published) */
    draft?: boolean
    /** Relationship population depth (default: 2) */
    depth?: number
  },
): Promise<Config["collections"][T] | null> {
  const payload = await getPayloadClient()
  const { draft = false, depth = 2 } = options ?? {}

  const result = await payload.find({
    collection,
    overrideAccess: false,
    where: {
      slug: { equals: slug },
    },
    depth,
    limit: 1,
    draft,
  })

  return result.docs[0] as Config["collections"][T] ?? null
}

/**
 * Find a single document by a custom field value.
 * Returns the document if found, or null if not found.
 *
 * Useful for collections that use a field other than `slug` for routing,
 * such as `title`, `handle`, or `sku`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * import { findByField } from '@/lib/payload'
 * import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
 *
 * export default async function ProductPage({ params }) {
 *   const { sku } = await params
 *   const product = await findByField('products', 'sku', sku)
 *   if (!product) notFound()
 *   return <Product data={product} />
 * }
 * ```
 */
export async function findByField<T extends CollectionSlug>(
  collection: T,
  field: string,
  value: string,
  options?: {
    /** Include draft documents (default: false, only published) */
    draft?: boolean
    /** Relationship population depth (default: 2) */
    depth?: number
  },
): Promise<Config["collections"][T] | null> {
  const payload = await getPayloadClient()
  const { draft = false, depth = 2 } = options ?? {}

  const result = await payload.find({
    collection,
    overrideAccess: false,
    where: {
      [field]: { equals: value },
    },
    depth,
    limit: 1,
    draft,
  })

  return result.docs[0] as Config["collections"][T] ?? null
}

Evaluating migration plan

I need to explain the impact of the migration plan carefully. The tool for asking specific questions isn’t available, but I can consider equivalent options even if it doesn’t allow for freeform input. Since deleting an email would cause data loss, I want to find a way to preserve the email while adding required unique identifiers. It could be better to assign temporary IDs based on record ID and ensure existing emails are retained in a legacy field. I’m pondering how to balance these changes effectively.

Refining email migration

I’m considering migrating emails to a legacy field while adding the voter ID and address as optional for old documents. However, existing records wouldn’t have those IDs and addresses. The user might be fine with deleting test records, but I need to clarify the plan: removing the email field means two stored email values become invalid. I want to keep existing registrations with the optional legacy email hidden, making voter ID and address required in the public form. They asked for a replacement, so I need clear confirmation on options to proceed.

Planning schema updates

I need to explain the plan clearly: I want to update the frontend and schema while keeping the existing email as a hidden, read-only legacy field to prevent data loss. I'm also adding optional voter ID and address fields since existing documents lack values, enforcing that new registrations are required to be unique. However, since the user requested a replacement, I should confirm whether they want a destructive change or prefer to preserve the current data. It's important to handle their decision carefully and keep sensitive information private!

The voters collection currently contains 2 registered voters, and both records rely on the required unique email field. Replacing it directly would remove those stored email values, while the existing records have no voter ID or address to backfill.

Proposed change:

  • Remove email from the voter schema and registration form.
  • Add a required, unique voterId.
  • Add a required address.
  • Existing voter records cannot be migrated accurately because their voter IDs and addresses are unknown, so those two records may become invalid and would need to be registered again.
  • Existing vote records and private voting codes will otherwise remain unchanged.
